- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model shows gradual upward trend, overestimate early peaks; correct by reducing slope after 3–5 consecutive bullish sentiment days.
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% of recent 7-day average if bearish sentiment persists.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots — cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for next 3–5 days unless sentiment remains bullish.
- When official events are frequent and supply net is negative, model underestimates volatility — increase forecast variance by 10–20% if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if recent sentiment is trending, especially after auction events.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, mean reversion is strong — if model shows >10% deviation from 30d moving average, adjust toward historical mean unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- When bullish sentiment is high but official supply net is negative, model often overestimates upside — reduce forecast by 3–5% if supply net is < -15 and sentiment > 0.75.
- If sentiment is bearish and model shows flat or rising trend, force downward correction — reduce forecast by 2–4% per day if sentiment < -0.5 and supply net < -10.
